summary.oneLiner: International Gemological Institute is one of the world's largest independent gemstone and jewelry certification bodies — a Blackstone portfolio company operating 36 laboratories and 21 gemological schools across 10 countries and the market leader in lab-grown diamond certification.
summary.business: IGI is a global provider of independent certification and grading services for diamonds, color gemstones and jewelry, established in 1975 in Antwerp, Belgium. Its core business is the issuance of certification reports that verify the quality, authenticity and key characteristics of diamonds, color gemstones and jewelry, serving more than 7,500 customers globally including diamond growers, wholesalers, jewelry manufacturers, retailers and leading international jewelry brands. Alongside its laboratory operations IGI runs a global education business offering courses in gemology and jewelry …

currentContext.expansion: IGI's expansion in 2025-26 was inorganic and footprint-led rather than plant-led, consistent with an asset-light laboratory model. The defining step was the completed acquisition of American Gemological Laboratories (AGL), described as a strategic expansion of the Company's global colored gemstone certification capabilities; the transaction combines IGI's global footprint, operational scale and infrastructure with AGL's established scientific expertise in colored gemstone analysis, strengthening IGI's presence in the United States — one of the largest markets for fine jewelry and colored gemstones — while reinforcing linkages with India as a key global hub for gemstone manufacturing, and is expected to deliver improved market access and operational synergies. The underlying platform being expanded is a network of 36 laboratories and 21 gemological schools spanning major jewelry hubs in India, USA, China, the UAE and Europe. No new laboratory construction project, commissioning date or capex programme is named in the routed sections; the only capital-deployment detail disclosed is that IPO proceeds were applied to the acquisition of the IGI Belgium Group and IGI Netherlands Group from the Promoter and to general corporate purposes, monitored by ICRA Limited. The remainder of the routed capacity narrative is industry rather than company capacity: Indian lab-grown diamond growers have increased capacity consistently, the domestic CVD reactor base is expanding, manufacturers are planning to double production capacity over the next three years to meet rising demand, and India accounts for roughly 35% of global rough LGD output and about 28.6% of global LGD exports. IGI positions itself as the beneficiary of that third-party capacity build-out, citing deep integration with key growers including in-factory grading, which provides visibility on rising volumes, and rising volumes plus operational efficiencies as the source of operating leverage.

risks.note: Economic volatility, geopolitical tensions and regulatory changes could influence consumer demand and affect business performance across markets; the Company relies on its diversified geographic presence and strong industry positioning for resilience.

risks.risk: Geographical revenue concentration in Gujarat and Maharashtra
risks.note: A significant share of revenue is concentrated in key regions such as Gujarat and Maharashtra, exposing the business to regional economic fluctuations and industry disruptions; mitigation is expansion into new regions and global markets to diversify the customer base.

risks.risk: Operational and reputational risk in grading judgment
risks.note: Gem grading relies on expert judgment, so inconsistencies or errors may impact IGI's reputation and customer confidence — the core asset of a certification business; mitigated through standardized grading processes, rigorous gemologist training, AI-supported grading tools and calibrated evaluation protocols.

risks.risk: Competition from global laboratories and new certification providers
risks.note: Increasing competition from established global laboratories and emerging certification providers may lead to pricing pressure and market share challenges; countered by investment in advanced grading technologies, brand credibility and global expansion.

risks.risk: Human resources — attracting and retaining skilled gemologists
risks.note: Difficulty in attracting, training and retaining skilled gemologists could affect operational efficiency, grading accuracy and service quality; addressed through competitive compensation, career development and specialized training programmes.

risks.risk: Security and insurance risk over client goods in custody and transit
risks.note: Theft, fraud or damage to diamonds, jewelry and gemstones during certification or transportation could result in financial loss and reputational harm; mitigated through robust security systems, comprehensive insurance coverage and advanced tracking technologies.

risks.risk: Technological risk — failure to adopt emerging grading technology
risks.note: Failure to adopt emerging technologies such as advanced spectroscopy, automation or AI could affect operational efficiency, competitiveness and market positioning. The BRSR additionally flags cybersecurity and data privacy as a material risk, where threats and system vulnerabilities could compromise the security, integrity and availability of client and company data.

risks.risk: Regulatory risk — licences, approvals and evolving compliance frameworks
risks.note: Dependence on licences, approvals and compliance with evolving regulatory frameworks means delays or non-compliance could disrupt business operations, restrict market access and harm reputation; managed through continuous monitoring of regulatory developments, timely renewals, employee training and periodic compliance audits.

one-line thesis: Strong start to FY27: consolidated certification revenue +23% (volume +17%), EBITDA +29% (60.4% margin, +270 bps), PAT +31% — LGD (loose +25%, jewellery +44%) and the AGL coloured-stone consolidation (+200% gemstones) drive growth, while natural-diamond loose (+6%) is the strategic focus for share gains. The moat thesis holds: "an IGI certificate makes a lab-grown diamond a diamond" — grower capacity is doubling, and every stone needs certifying. Guidance (conservatively) held at 15% revenue / 20% EBITDA growth + AGL.

AGL = +3% revenue, +2% EBITDA incremental. India ASP INR 870 (vs 861 — stable). Marketing (IPL/Gujarat Titans sponsorship) ~INR 5 cr, front-loaded.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue growth: 15%** on base business + **~2–3% from AGL** for FY27 (held despite a 23% Q1 — deliberately conservative, "early days").
- **EBITDA growth: 20%** (FY27); consolidated EBITDA margin to **improve ~100 bps by year-end** (from ~61% FY26).
- **India standalone EBITDA margin to stabilise in the ~70% range** as discretionary (IPL/brand) spends moderate.
- Pricing expected **stable** (unchanged since the April–May 2024 LGD correction); realisation drift is mix/caratage, not list-price.
order book & pipeline: N/A (volume-throughput certification business, no order book). Volume drivers: LGD grower capacity additions, rising consumer acceptance/affordability of LGD, ND-loose share gains (new customers + wallet share), AGL coloured-stone cross-sell + geographic expansion.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **LGD** (loose +25%, jewellery +44%): primary volume engine; grower capacity/"business" expected to double over ~3 years.
- **Natural diamonds** (loose +6%, jewellery +2%): strategic priority for global share (India already #1); LGD's new consumer base up-trading into IGI-certified ND.
- **AGL (coloured stones):** consolidation drove gemstones +200%; plan to take AGL global (start Jaipur collection window + mobile labs), cross-sell; +3% revenue / +2% EBITDA this quarter.
- **International subs:** US, Belgium (+Italy commenced), Dubai, China (Shanghai/Shenzhen) — retail-engagement/lead-gen offices earning commission from India; margins improving on operating leverage.
growth verticals / optionality:
- Coloured gemstones (AGL) as a new TAM beyond diamonds; global roll-out.
- ND-loose global share gains (multiplier on realisation).
- LGD jewellery (fast-growing, incl. India); larger-caratage CVD stones (75-carat single stone certified last year) lifting mix.
- AI/ML for turnaround-time reduction and workforce optimisation.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Trust/network moat:** "without certification, [an LGD] can be considered just a piece of glass … IGI gives the authenticity" — certification is the indispensable trust layer.
- **Concentration cuts both ways but favours IGI:** ~10–14 large LGD growers ≈ 80% of India's grown stones (≈40–50% of IGI revenue), yet all are reliant on IGI certification → pricing has held stable (INR 80–120/carat band) for ~2 years despite scale.
- **One-IGI operating leverage:** India manufacturing/certifying strength (70–74% standalone EBITDA margin) + overseas retail lead-gen = expanding consolidated margins; interdependence is the defensible structure.
- **Only listed pure-play** certification player (declines segment carat disclosures on competitive grounds).
margins & cost dynamics:
- Consol EBITDA margin 60.4% (+270 bps); India standalone 68.8% (lower YoY due to commission payouts to overseas geographies + front-loaded IPL/brand spend + headcount).
- Realisation +5% (AGL +3%, base +2% via caratage/mix); underlying list pricing stable.
- Operating leverage as volumes scale is the core margin lever, in India and overseas.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): - Incremental capex consistent with volume scale-up (D&A step-up); finance cost up on additional office rentals. Debt-free. AGL integration + global mobile-lab/collection-window expansion the main growth spend. No large discrete capex quantified.
capital allocation:
- Debt-free; AGL acquisition (coloured stones) the notable inorganic move — now contributing.
- Discretionary brand investment (IPL sponsorship, leadership hires) framed as long-haul brand-building; expected to moderate.
risks & watch-items:
- **LGD pricing/realisation** as grower capacity doubles — mgmt insists price stable (grower margins 10–12% per IGI vs "6–10%" cited from its own deck); watch for negotiation pressure.
- **Customer concentration:** ~8–10 growers ≈ 40–50% of revenue.
- ND-jewellery softness (Q4 decline, +2% now) — mix swings dent realisation.
- Guidance (15%/20%) far below Q1 delivery (23%/29%) — either conservative or an H2 slowdown signal.
- Discretionary-spend margin drag if brand investment doesn't moderate.
management quality / tone: Confident, franchise-proud; CEO Tehmasp Printer strong on the certification-moat narrative, CFO Eashwar Iyer precise on the ASP/caratage and one-IGI margin mechanics. Deliberately conservative on guidance. Declined competitively sensitive detail (segment carats). Handled repeated realisation/negotiation probing patiently.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Realisation rose **despite** an LGD-heavier mix — driven by **higher caratage** (LGD stones are >1–2 carat vs sub-carat ND pointers), so ND vs LGD per-report economics effectively converge; the usual "mix dilutes ASP" fear is offset by rising stone sizes.
- The bull case is a **flywheel**: LGD's affordability creates new consumers → exposed to IGI certification → up-trade into IGI-certified natural diamonds (ND-loose global growth is the tell).
- India standalone margin (68.8%) looks "down," but that's the **one-IGI commission transfer** to overseas lead-gen offices — consolidated margin (60.4%, +270 bps) is the correct lens (mgmt insists).
- Held guidance at 15%/20% after a 23%/29% quarter — read as sandbagging or an explicit flag that H2 normalises.
